title: Samtec Puts AI's Interconnect Bottleneck on Display at ECOC and AI Infra Summit - Semiwiki
gist: Samtec is using the AI Infra Summit (Sept 15-17, Santa Clara) and ECOC 2026 (Sept 21-23, Málaga) to argue that AI infrastructure performance is now bottlenecked by copper/optical interconnect rather than accelerator speed alone, showcasing its Si-Fly HD CPX co-packaged architecture targeting 224/448-Gbps PAM4/PAM6 signaling and joining a 39-company OIF interoperability demo.

themes.theme: Interconnect, Not Compute Alone, Gates AI Performance

insights.claim: Samtec's core argument at two major 2026 industry events is that faster accelerators alone will not determine next-generation AI infrastructure performance; the copper and optical links connecting chips, packages, boards, racks and data centers must scale in bandwidth, density and energy efficiency at the same pace.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Reinforces interconnect/optical-networking suppliers as a distinct AI infrastructure investment thesis alongside accelerator makers, since compute gains can be capped by link bandwidth.
insights.quote: Samtec is using two major 2026 industry events to make a clear engineering argument: faster accelerators alone will not determine the performance of next-generation artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

insights.claim: The broader message from Samtec's dual-event push is that AI's next performance gains depend on moving data efficiently, not merely calculating faster.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A framing investors can use to identify which AI infra sub-sector (interconnect/networking vs. compute silicon) is under-covered relative to its performance impact.
insights.quote: The broader message is that AI’s next performance gains depend on moving data efficiently, not merely calculating faster.

themes.theme: Si-Fly HD CPX: Co-Packaged Copper and Optics

insights.claim: Samtec will demonstrate PCI Express 5.0 running over FireFly optical cable assemblies, Si-Fly HD 224-Gbps PAM4 co-packaged and near-chip systems, and early Si-Fly HD technology targeting 448-Gbps PAM4 and PAM6 signaling at the AI Infra Summit (booth 304, Santa Clara Convention Center, Sept 15-17).
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: 448-Gbps PAM4/PAM6 signaling being demoed as 'early technology' marks the next generational interconnect speed tier to track for adoption timing.
insights.quote: The announced exhibits include PCI Express 5.0 running over FireFly optical cable assemblies, Si-Fly HD 224-Gbps PAM4 co-packaged and near-chip systems, and early Si-Fly HD technology targeting 448-Gbps PAM4 and PAM6 signaling.
insights.locator: paragraph on AI Infra Summit demos

insights.claim: The Si-Fly HD CPX architecture is an electrically pluggable platform for co-packaged copper and optics that fits on a 95-by-95-millimeter or smaller substrate, with an SFCM connector mounting directly to the package substrate and mating with Samtec's SFCC cable assembly or compatible optical assemblies.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A concrete physical form factor (95x95mm substrate footprint) that system architects can use to assess integration feasibility against competing co-packaged optics/copper standards.
insights.quote: Samtec describes it as an electrically pluggable platform for co-packaged copper and optics that can fit on a 95-by-95-millimeter or smaller substrate.

insights.claim: Moving the interconnect onto the package avoids the insertion loss associated with ball-grid-array breakouts and long printed-circuit-board traces, making a complete passive direct-attach-copper channel at 224 Gbps practical.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific engineering mechanism (avoiding BGA/PCB trace loss) enabling passive (retimer-free) 224G copper links — a cost and power advantage over active-retimed alternatives.
insights.quote: Moving the interconnect onto the package avoids the insertion loss associated with ball-grid-array breakouts and long printed-circuit-board traces, making a complete passive direct-attach-copper channel at 224 Gbps practical.

themes.theme: Signal Integrity Becomes the Binding Constraint at 224G+

insights.claim: At 224 Gbps, attenuation, crosstalk, reflections and jitter consume the channel budget quickly; designers can compensate with retimers and equalization, but every active component adds power, heat, latency, cost and potential failure points.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Each added active retimer in a 224G link chain is a direct tax on power and reliability budgets — a metric to compare across vendors' link architectures.
insights.quote: At 224 Gbps, attenuation, crosstalk, reflections and jitter consume the channel budget quickly. Designers can compensate with retimers and equalization, but every active component adds power, heat, latency, cost and potential failure points.

insights.claim: Shortening the electrical path and placing signal conversion closer to the silicon preserves signal quality while giving architects flexibility to use copper for short reaches and optics where distance or density makes electrical transmission inefficient.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A practical design heuristic (copper for short reach, optics for long/dense) for evaluating how any AI rack-scale interconnect roadmap should be architected.
insights.quote: Shortening the electrical path and placing conversion closer to the silicon preserves signal quality while giving architects the flexibility to use copper for short reaches and optics where distance or density makes electrical transmission inefficient.

insights.claim: Scale-up links join accelerators into a tightly coupled compute domain, while scale-out networks connect larger numbers of nodes; both require high throughput but differ in reach, latency, topology and power constraints.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Scale-up vs scale-out is a key segmentation for evaluating which interconnect technology (copper vs optical, pluggable vs co-packaged) wins in which part of an AI data center topology.
insights.quote: The distinction is critical: scale-up links join accelerators into a tightly coupled compute domain, while scale-out networks connect larger numbers of nodes. Both require high throughput, but their reach, latency, topology and power constraints differ.

themes.theme: Multivendor Interoperability as a Deployment Risk Reducer

insights.claim: Samtec is participating in the Optical Internetworking Forum's live interoperability demonstration at ECOC 2026, which OIF says will involve 39 member companies allowing components from different suppliers to operate together in realistic link configurations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A 39-company live interop demo is a concrete signal that 224G/448G interconnect standards are maturing toward deployable, multivendor status rather than remaining proprietary silos.
insights.quote: OIF says the showcase will involve 39 member companies, allowing components from different suppliers to operate together in realistic link configurations.

insights.claim: Interoperability is essential for AI infrastructure because no single vendor supplies the entire data path; accelerators, switch silicon, connectors, cables, optical engines, transceivers and test equipment must meet common electrical, optical and management expectations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Highlights standards-body work (OIF) as a bottleneck-reducing catalyst for hyperscaler AI buildouts, worth tracking alongside individual vendor product announcements.
insights.quote: Interoperability is essential for AI infrastructure because no single vendor supplies the entire data path.

insights.claim: OIF's work on 224G and 448G Common Electrical I/O, coherent optics, co-packaging, management interfaces and energy-efficient links helps reduce uncertainty for hyperscalers and equipment makers planning multigeneration platforms.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Standards convergence at 224G/448G lowers hyperscaler platform-planning risk, which should accelerate capex commitment timelines for next-gen AI racks.
insights.quote: OIF’s work on 224G and 448G Common Electrical I/O, coherent optics, co-packaging, management interfaces and energy-efficient links helps reduce uncertainty for hyperscalers and equipment makers planning multigeneration platforms.

insights.claim: Samtec is positioning itself beyond the traditional connector category, with a value proposition spanning from the package edge to external optical links, supported by signal-integrity expertise and pluggable architectures.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Samtec's expanding scope (package-to-system signal path) suggests it is competing more directly with optical-module and co-packaged-optics vendors, not just traditional connector makers.
insights.quote: Samtec positioning itself beyond the traditional connector category. Its value proposition spans the distance from the package edge to external optical links, supported by signal-integrity expertise and pluggable architectures.

insights.claim: For customers, Samtec's dense copper and optical systems can mean shorter design cycles, clearer upgrade paths and better utilization of costly compute silicon; for the industry, they help convert ambitious 224G and 448G roadmaps into deployable, multivendor systems.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Better utilization of costly compute silicon via improved interconnect is a direct margin/ROI lever for hyperscalers evaluating capex efficiency on GPU clusters.
insights.quote: For customers, that can mean shorter design cycles, clearer upgrade paths and better utilization of costly compute silicon.
